reasons: Covers the specific past bug and its fix.
Checks both light and dark paths and the edge cases with empty input.

terms.meaning: A number for how bright a color looks, used to decide if a background is dark.
A design mistake the generator warns the user about.
A test added after a bug is fixed, so the same bug cannot quietly return.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and sample records
sections.what: Loads the design functions under test and defines sample light and dark palettes and two sample styles, one dark-only and one that works in both modes.
sections.why: Gives each test a known, repeatable input.
sections.watch_out: The samples are copies of real data rows, so they must be updated by hand if the data changes.

sections.name: TestLuminance
sections.title: Brightness and background checks
sections.what: Checks that color codes of different lengths are read correctly, that bad input returns nothing, that dark and light backgrounds are classified correctly, and that a missing background is treated as not dark.
sections.why: The dark or light decision depends on these brightness results.
sections.watch_out: Bad or missing color data is quietly treated as light, so a data error could go unnoticed.

sections.name: TestModeResolution
sections.title: Mode choice checks
sections.what: Checks that a dark-only style is detected, that a dual-mode style is not, that dark-related words in a query are detected, and that either a dark style or a dark query selects dark mode.
sections.why: Mode is chosen from two signals, so each signal needs its own check.
sections.watch_out: The query keyword list decides the mode, so adding or removing a keyword changes results across the app.

sections.name: TestPaletteSelection
sections.title: Palette choice checks
sections.what: Checks that dark mode skips light palettes, falls back to the top result when no dark palette exists, and that light mode keeps the top result.
sections.why: Makes sure the chosen palette matches the chosen mode.
sections.watch_out: The fallback can return a light palette in dark mode, which is the bug this file guards against.

sections.name: TestAntiPatternGating
sections.title: Warning filter checks
sections.what: Checks that the dark-mode warning clause is removed in dark mode while other warnings stay, that light mode leaves warnings unchanged, and that empty input stays empty.
sections.why: Stops the design output from warning against the very mode it chose.
sections.watch_out: The filter works on text matching, so rewording the warning in the data can make it stop being removed.

sections.name: TestEndToEndCoherence
sections.title: End to end dark and light checks
sections.what: Runs the full generator on a dark query and checks that the background is dark, the text is lighter than the background, and no dark-mode warning appears. A light query is checked to keep a light background.
sections.why: Confirms the separate pieces work together in the final output.
sections.watch_out: These checks depend on the current data, so a data update can change the result without any code change.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Running the design tests directly
sections.what: Lets you run every test in this file as a program, with more detailed output: each test name is printed as it runs, so you can see which checks passed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the verbose setting helps when reading results by hand. Reason not stated in the code beyond that.

summary: Automatic checks that the light or dark color mode is chosen once and then applied consistently to style, color palette and warnings.
purpose: Prevents a dark style from being paired with a light palette and a contradictory anti-pattern warning.
why: Likely reason: a past bug (issue 428) returned mismatched choices because each part was picked separately.
how: 1) Adds the scripts folder to the import path. 2) Loads sample light and dark palettes and a dark-only style. 3) Checks brightness reading, mode detection from the style and the query text, palette choice, warning filtering and the full generator output.
inputs: Sample palettes and styles written into the test file, plus the helper functions in design_system.
outputs: A pass or fail report for each check.
risks: Some sample values are copied from the shipped data. If that data changes, the samples may stop matching it, and the tests would still pass.
debug: If a mode check fails, look at the mode helper functions in design_system. If a palette check fails, check how the palette list is filtered. The end-to-end group is the best place to find a mismatch across the whole output.
